Base class for objects participating in Wt's signal/slot system. Manages lifetime of child WObject instances, provides unique IDs, object naming, and support for stateless slot learning/JavaScript implementations. It inherits from Wt::Core::observable. Construction is default, copy is disabled, destruction virtual. It owns children via unique_ptr and manages stateless slot implementations. Threaded builds use atomic for id generation.

functions.signature:
template <typename T, typename... Args>
[[deprecated("Wt::cpp14::make_unique has been marked as deprecated and will be removed in the future, use std::make_unique instead.")]]
auto Wt::cpp14::make_unique(Args&&... args) -> decltype(std::make_unique<T, Args...>(std::forward<Args>(args)...))
functions.description: Creates a std::unique_ptr<T> by perfectly forwarding the provided constructor arguments to T’s constructor. functions.name: Wt::WObject::addChild

requirements: Caller transfers ownership of the child via a std::unique_ptr; after the call, the passed unique_ptr must not be used.
The child must be a WObject (or derived).

functions.name: Wt::WObject::removeChild
functions.description: Removes a child WObject from this parent, returning ownership to the caller. If the specified pointer is a child, ownership of exactly that object is returned; otherwise, a null unique_ptr is returned.

functions.name: Wt::WObject::resetLearnedSlots
functions.description: Clears all learned stateless implementations for slots previously declared stateless. Use this when changes invalidate the assumption that these slots are stateless or their visual effect has changed.

functions.name: Wt::WObject::resetLearnedSlot
functions.description: Clears the learned stateless implementation for a specific slot method previously declared stateless. Use this when the slot’s effect is no longer invariant and must be relearned.
requirements: This must be called with a pointer to a member function of T with signature void (T::*)().
The dynamic type of this must be convertible to T* (the implementation asserts dynamic_cast<T*>(this)).

functions.name: Wt::WObject::implementStateless
functions.description: Declares a slot method as stateless and enables auto-learning of a client-side JavaScript implementation upon first invocation of the event. The C++ slot continues to run; the learned JS only optimizes the visual effect latency.
requirements: method must be a pointer to a member function of T with signature void (T::*)().
The dynamic type of this must be convertible to T* (the implementation asserts dynamic_cast<T*>(this)).
The slot’s visual effect must not depend on application state (i.e., must be stateless) until resetLearnedSlot()/resetLearnedSlots() is called.
Call this before any EventSignal connects to the slot to ensure the stateless implementation is recognized for that connection.

functions.name: Wt::WObject::isNotStateless
functions.description: Marks the current function context as not stateless. Use within code paths that may be invoked from a stateless-marked function but that have state-dependent effects, to prevent pre-learning and revert to server-side updates.

functions.name: Wt::WObject::implementJavaScript
functions.signature:
template <class T>
Wt::WStatelessSlot* Wt::WObject::implementJavaScript(void (T::*method)(), const std::string& jsCode)
functions.description: Provides an explicit JavaScript implementation for a slot method. If JavaScript is available, the JS code will be used on the client for visual effects, bypassing auto-learning. The C++ slot still executes on the server.
requirements: method must be a pointer to a member function of T with signature void (T::*)().
The dynamic type of this must be convertible to T* (the implementation asserts dynamic_cast<T*>(this)).
jsCode must be one or more valid JavaScript statements implementing the visual effect intended for the slot.

import random
import struct
import string
from typing import List

# This generator targets FUZZ_PARAM_STR inputs used across the stubs.
# The stubs exercise WString construction (with CharEncoding), UTF-8 validation,
# JavaScript snippets, URLs, names/identifiers, meta headers, and attribute values.
# We therefore build a small corpus container format carrying multiple strings,
# each tuned to trigger diverse code paths. The fuzzer harness will read them
# sequentially as FUZZ_PARAM_STR().
#
# Container format (little endian):
#   u16 count
#   repeated count times:
#     u16 length
#     bytes[length]
#
# Each entry is <= 512 bytes; total buffer <= 4096 bytes.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096
MAX_ENTRY = 512

def _rnd_bytes(r: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(r.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))

def _utf8_valid_snippet(r: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    # Build valid UTF-8 by composing code points across ranges
    length = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    out = bytearray()
    while len(out) < length:
        choice = r.randint(0, 9)
        if choice <= 4:
            # ASCII
            out.append(r.choice([32, 33, 34, 39, 44, 45, 46, 47, 58, 59, 61, 63] + list(range(48, 58)) + list(range(65,91)) + list(range(97,123))))
        elif choice <= 6:
            # 2-byte
            cp = r.randint(0x80, 0x7FF)
            out.extend(bytes([0xC0 | (cp >> 6), 0x80 | (cp & 0x3F)]))
        elif choice <= 8:
            # 3-byte (avoid surrogates)
            cp = r.randint(0x800, 0xD7FF)
            out.extend(bytes([0xE0 | (cp >> 12), 0x80 | ((cp >> 6) & 0x3F), 0x80 | (cp & 0x3F)]))
        else:
            # 4-byte up to U+10FFFF
            cp = r.randint(0x10000, 0x10FFFF)
            out.extend(bytes([
                0xF0 | (cp >> 18),
                0x80 | ((cp >> 12) & 0x3F),
                0x80 | ((cp >> 6) & 0x3F),
                0x80 | (cp & 0x3F)
            ]))
    return bytes(out[:length])

def _safe_identifier(r: random.Random, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    first = r.choice(string.ascii_letters + '_$')
    rest_len = r.randint(0, max_len-1)
    rest = ''.join(r.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + '_$') for _ in range(rest_len))
    return (first + rest).encode('ascii')

def _safe_attr_name(r: random.Random, prefix: str, max_rand: int) -> bytes:
    raw = ''.join(r.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + '-_') for _ in range(r.randint(1, max_rand)))
    return (prefix + raw).encode('ascii')

def _url_candidate(r: random.Random, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    schemes = [b"http://", b"https://", b"//", b"/", b"data:", b"about:"]
    scheme = r.choice(schemes)
    host = b""
    if scheme in (b"http://", b"https://", b"//"):
        labels = [bytes(''.join(r.choice(string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits) for _ in range(r.randint(1,8))), 'ascii') for _ in range(r.randint(1,3))]
        host = b".".join(labels) + b".test"
        path = b"/" + b"/".join(_rnd_bytes(r, r.randint(1,4)).hex().encode('ascii') for _ in range(r.randint(0,3)))
        tail = host + path
    elif scheme == b"/":
        tail = b"api/" + _rnd_bytes(r, 4).hex().encode('ascii')
    else:
        tail = _rnd_bytes(r, r.randint(4, 16)).hex().encode('ascii')
    q = b""
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        q = b"?k=" + _rnd_bytes(r, 3).hex().encode('ascii')
    url = scheme + tail + q
    return url[:max_len]

def _js_snippet(r: random.Random, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    pieces = [
        b"void 0;",
        b"var x=1;",
        b"x+=2;",
        b"(function(){return x;})();",
        b"/*fuzz*/",
        b"if(x){x--;}",
    ]
    out = b" ".join(r.choices(pieces, k=r.randint(1,5)))
    # sprinkle safe printable bytes
    extra = ''.join(r.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + ' _+-*/') for _ in range(r.randint(0, 16))).encode('ascii')
    s = out + b" " + extra
    return s[:max_len]

def _bounded(r: random.Random, data: bytes, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    if len(data) > max_len:
        return data[:max_len]
    return data

def _meta_rel(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    rels = [b"stylesheet", b"preload", b"icon", b"apple-touch-icon"]
    return r.choice(rels)

def _maybe_empty(r: random.Random, val: bytes) -> bytes:
    return b"" if r.random() < 0.34 else val

def _assemble(entries: List[bytes]) -> bytes:
    # Pack u16 count and u16 length per entry
    header = struct.pack('<H', len(entries))
    chunks = [header]
    for e in entries:
        chunks.append(struct.pack('<H', len(e)))
        chunks.append(e)
    blob = b"".join(chunks)
    return blob[:MAX_TOTAL]

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    entries: List[bytes] = []

    # 1) Generic arbitrary bytes (exercise generic std::string, including NULs)
    entries.append(_rnd_bytes(r, r.randint(0, 64)))
    entries.append(_rnd_bytes(r, r.randint(5, 32)) + b"\x00middle\x00end")

    # 2) Valid UTF-8 strings (for fromUTF8 with checkValid=true)
    entries.append(_utf8_valid_snippet(r, 1, 80))
    entries.append(_utf8_valid_snippet(r, 20, 120))

    # 3) Likely invalid UTF-8 to pair with checkValid=false path
    inv = bytearray(_rnd_bytes(r, r.randint(10, 40)))
    if inv:
        # introduce some overlong/isolated continuation bytes
        for i in range(0, len(inv), r.randint(3,7)):
            inv[i] = r.randint(0x80, 0xBF)
    entries.append(bytes(inv))

    # 4) Names/identifiers for object names and JS function names
    entries.append(_bounded(r, _safe_identifier(r, 20), 64))
    entries.append(_bounded(r, _safe_identifier(r, 24), 64))

    # 5) Attribute names and values (html/body attributes)
    entries.append(_bounded(r, _safe_attr_name(r, 'data-fuzz-', 12), 32))
    val = _utf8_valid_snippet(r, 0, 64).replace(b"'", b"\\'").replace(b'\"', b'\\\"')
    entries.append(val)

    # 6) URLs for redirect/require/makeAbsoluteUrl/encodeUntrustedUrl
    for _ in range(4):
        entries.append(_url_candidate(r, 180))

    # 7) JavaScript payloads for doJavaScript/addAutoJavaScript/declareJavaScriptFunction body
    for _ in range(3):
        entries.append(_js_snippet(r, 180))

    # 8) Meta header components: name, content (UTF-8), lang, userAgent, rel
    name = _bounded(r, _utf8_valid_snippet(r, 3, 20), 64)
    content = _bounded(r, _utf8_valid_snippet(r, 5, 120), 256)
    lang = _maybe_empty(r, r.choice([b"en", b"en-US", b"fr", b"de"]))
    ua = _maybe_empty(r, b"Mozilla/5.0 (fuzz)")
    entries.extend([name, content, lang, ua, _meta_rel(r)])

    # 9) Theme names (empty or small name)
    entries.append(b"" if r.random() < 0.25 else _bounded(r, _utf8_valid_snippet(r, 3, 16), 32))

    # 10) Filenames or symbols for require()
    entries.append(_bounded(r, _safe_identifier(r, 16), 24))

    # 11) Short keys for configuration property lookups
    entries.append(_bounded(r, _safe_identifier(r, 16), 48))

    # 12) Additional arbitrary small blobs to feed remaining FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls
    for _ in range(r.randint(4, 8)):
        choice = r.randint(0, 4)
        if choice == 0:
            entries.append(_rnd_bytes(r, r.randint(0, 40)))
        elif choice == 1:
            entries.append(_utf8_valid_snippet(r, 1, 40))
        elif choice == 2:
            entries.append(_url_candidate(r, 96))
        elif choice == 3:
            entries.append(_js_snippet(r, 96))
        else:
            entries.append(_safe_identifier(r, 18))

    # Ensure size limits per entry
    entries = [e[:MAX_ENTRY] for e in entries]

    buf = _assemble(entries)
    # Guarantee non-empty and within cap
    if not buf:
        buf = struct.pack('<H', 0)
    return buf

import random
import struct
import string
from typing import List

# Target data type: UTF-8 string
# Fuzzer stubs consume FUZZ_PARAM_STR() primarily as UTF-8 text for WString::fromUTF8 and Wt::utf8,
# and as general std::string inputs for WString constructors and MetaHeader fields. We therefore
# generate valid and interesting UTF-8 payloads that exercise:
# - ASCII control, printable, and whitespace
# - Multilingual characters across planes (BMP and supplementary planes via surrogate pairs in UTF-16, encoded correctly in UTF-8)
# - Mixed scripts, combining marks, direction markers, emoji, variation selectors
# - Different lengths, including empty and boundary-ish sizes (but < 4096)
# The fuzzer framework typically maps the single generated buffer to multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR() calls
# by slicing or reusing; to help, we pack several UTF-8 strings with length prefixes so the harness
# can pull distinct segments when it requests additional FUZZ_PARAM_STR() calls.
#
# Buffer format we emit:
#   [count:u8]
#   repeat count times:
#     [len:u16 little endian][payload bytes of that length]
# Total size <= 4096.
# Each payload is valid UTF-8.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096
MAX_SEG = 512

ASCII_PRINTABLE = ''.join(chr(c) for c in range(0x20, 0x7F))
ASCII_CONTROL = ''.join(chr(c) for c in list(range(0x00, 0x20)) + [0x7F])
WHITESPACE = " \t\r\n\v\f"

# A curated set of Unicode ranges to sample from
RANGES = [
    (0x00A0, 0x00FF),   # Latin-1 supplement
    (0x0100, 0x017F),   # Latin Extended-A
    (0x0370, 0x03FF),   # Greek
    (0x0400, 0x04FF),   # Cyrillic
    (0x0590, 0x05FF),   # Hebrew
    (0x0600, 0x06FF),   # Arabic
    (0x0900, 0x097F),   # Devanagari
    (0x3040, 0x309F),   # Hiragana
    (0x30A0, 0x30FF),   # Katakana
    (0x4E00, 0x9FFF),   # CJK Unified Ideographs
    (0x1F300, 0x1F5FF), # Misc Symbols & Pictographs (emoji block)
    (0x1F600, 0x1F64F), # Emoticons
    (0x1F900, 0x1F9FF), # Supplemental Symbols and Pictographs
]

COMBINING_MARKS = [
    0x0301, 0x0300, 0x0308, 0x0303, 0x0327, 0x0323, 0x0302, 0x030A
]

DIRECTIONAL_MARKS = [
    0x200E, # LRM
    0x200F, # RLM
    0x202A, # LRE
    0x202B, # RLE
    0x202C, # PDF
    0x202D, # LRO
    0x202E, # RLO
]

VARIATION_SELECTORS = [
    0xFE0E, 0xFE0F
]

ZW_CHARS = [
    0x200B, # ZWSP
    0x200C, # ZWNJ
    0x200D, # ZWJ
    0x2060, # WJ
]

URL_LIKE = [
    "https://example.com/path?query=1#frag",
    "mailto:user@example.org",
    "data:text/plain,hello%20world",
    "ws://localhost:8080/socket",
]

META_NAMES = [
    "viewport", "description", "keywords", "theme-color", "referrer", "content-type",
]

def _rand_ascii(rnd: random.Random, length: int) -> str:
    # Include printable with some whitespace; avoid embedded NUL in Python str
    chars = ASCII_PRINTABLE + WHITESPACE
    return ''.join(rnd.choice(chars) for _ in range(length))

def _rand_controls(rnd: random.Random, length: int) -> str:
    # Mix control with a few printable to keep it readable-ish
    chars = ASCII_CONTROL + ASCII_PRINTABLE
    return ''.join(rnd.choice(chars) for _ in range(length))

def _rand_from_range(rnd: random.Random, r) -> str:
    start, end = r
    code = rnd.randint(start, end)
    # Avoid unassigned surrogates etc. Python will handle astral properly
    return chr(code)

def _rand_unicode(rnd: random.Random, length: int) -> str:
    s = []
    for _ in range(length):
        r = rnd.choice(RANGES)
        s.append(_rand_from_range(rnd, r))
        # Occasionally add combining mark
        if rnd.random() < 0.15:
            s.append(chr(rnd.choice(COMBINING_MARKS)))
    return ''.join(s)

def _emoji_sequence(rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    # Build some common emoji sequences (flags, skin tones, ZWJ sequences)
    base = rnd.choice([
        0x1F466, # boy
        0x1F467, # girl
        0x1F9D1, # person
        0x1F600, # grinning
        0x1F4BB, # laptop
        0x1F468, # man
        0x1F469, # woman
    ])
    seq = [chr(base)]
    # Optional skin tone
    if rnd.random() < 0.5:
        seq.append(chr(rnd.randint(0x1F3FB, 0x1F3FF)))
    # Optional ZWJ join with another emoji
    if rnd.random() < 0.5:
        seq.append(chr(0x200D))
        seq.append(chr(rnd.choice([0x1F4BC, 0x1F680, 0x1F9AF, 0x1F33E])))
    # Optional variation selector
    if rnd.random() < 0.4:
        seq.append(chr(rnd.choice(VARIATION_SELECTORS)))
    return ''.join(seq)

def _mixed_utf8_sample(rnd: random.Random, target_len: int) -> str:
    parts: List[str] = []
    while len(''.join(parts)) < target_len:
        choice = rnd.random()
        if choice < 0.15:
            parts.append(_emoji_sequence(rnd))
        elif choice < 0.35:
            parts.append(_rand_unicode(rnd, rnd.randint(1, 6)))
        elif choice < 0.55:
            parts.append(_rand_ascii(rnd, rnd.randint(1, 10)))
        elif choice < 0.7:
            parts.append(chr(rnd.choice(DIRECTIONAL_MARKS)))
        elif choice < 0.85:
            parts.append(chr(rnd.choice(ZW_CHARS)))
        else:
            parts.append(_rand_controls(rnd, rnd.randint(1, 6)))
    return ''.join(parts)[:target_len]

def _meta_like(rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    name = rnd.choice(META_NAMES)
    if name == "viewport":
        return "width=device-width, initial-scale=" + str(rnd.choice(["1.0", "1.5", "2.0"]))
    if name == "theme-color":
        return rnd.choice(["#ffffff", "#000000", "#ff5722", "#2196f3"])
    if name == "referrer":
        return rnd.choice(["no-referrer", "strict-origin-when-cross-origin", "origin"]) 
    if name == "content-type":
        return "text/html; charset=UTF-8"
    if name == "description":
        return _mixed_utf8_sample(rnd, rnd.randint(20, 120))
    if name == "keywords":
        words = ["wt", "webtoolkit", "gui", "widgets", "c++", "server-side", "ajax"]
        rnd.shuffle(words)
        return ','.join(words[:rnd.randint(3, 6)])
    return name

def _bounded_utf8_bytes(s: str, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    b = s.encode('utf-8', 'strict')
    if len(b) <= max_len:
        return b
    # Truncate safely: back off to a character boundary by encoding progressively
    out = bytearray()
    for ch in s:
        cb = ch.encode('utf-8')
        if len(out) + len(cb) > max_len:
            break
        out.extend(cb)
    return bytes(out)

def _make_segments(rnd: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    segs: List[bytes] = []
    # Always include some canonical small cases first
    canon = [
        "",                                 # empty
        "ASCII",                            # simple
        "Hello, 世界",                       # BMP CJK
        "مرحبا",                             # Arabic
        "שלום",                              # Hebrew RTL
        "नमस्ते",                             # Devanagari
        "😊",                                 # emoji
        "A\u0308".encode('utf-8').decode('utf-8'), # A + combining diaeresis
    ]
    for s in canon:
        segs.append(_bounded_utf8_bytes(s, min(64, MAX_SEG)))

    # URL-like and meta-like content that maps to addMetaHeader/name/url scenarios
    segs.append(_bounded_utf8_bytes(rnd.choice(URL_LIKE), 256))
    segs.append(_bounded_utf8_bytes(rnd.choice(META_NAMES), 64))
    segs.append(_bounded_utf8_bytes(_meta_like(rnd), 256))

    # A few randomized mixed segments of varying sizes
    for _ in range(rnd.randint(5, 12)):
        target = rnd.choice([16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 384, 512])
        target = min(target, MAX_SEG)
        seg = _mixed_utf8_sample(rnd, rnd.randint(max(1, target//2), target))
        segs.append(_bounded_utf8_bytes(seg, target))

    # Ensure at least one longish paragraph with newlines/tabs
    para = []
    for _ in range(rnd.randint(3, 8)):
        para.append(_mixed_utf8_sample(rnd, rnd.randint(20, 80)))
    segs.append(_bounded_utf8_bytes('\n'.join(para), 512))

    # Deduplicate overly similar empties while preserving at least one empty
    seen_nonempty = set()
    uniq: List[bytes] = []
    empty_kept = False
    for b in segs:
        if not b and not empty_kept:
            uniq.append(b)
            empty_kept = True
        elif b:
            if b not in seen_nonempty:
                seen_nonempty.add(b)
                uniq.append(b)
    return uniq

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)
    segments = _make_segments(rnd)

    # Shuffle to vary ordering by seed
    rnd.shuffle(segments)

    # Pack with count and 16-bit lengths; ensure total <= MAX_TOTAL
    out = bytearray()
    out.append(0)  # placeholder for count
    count = 0
    for seg in segments:
        entry = struct.pack('<H', len(seg)) + seg
        if 1 + len(out) + len(entry) > MAX_TOTAL:
            break
        out.extend(entry)
        count += 1
        if count >= 255:
            break
    out[0] = count & 0xFF

    return bytes(out)
